Large language models are improving at an astonishing pace. Earlier this year we were still laughing at how dumb they were; now it’s a different story. If you spell out the requirements clearly, the error rate is manageable.

The most common problems:

- When you add a new requirement, it plants bugs in the existing code. You should be able to prevent that with instructions or rules, though I haven’t tried it yet.

- If it misunderstands a new requirement the first time, then even if you correct it straight away, it tends to fall back on brute force and piles on more code. Refactoring gets harder, and so does rolling back, so it’s best to commit as you go.
